title: Lightweight KV-hit Susceptibility Prober and Rollback Advisor
creator: Aisha Verma
description: Build a lightweight probing service that intermittently replays live requests both with prefetched/KV-cached execution and without cache (decached) to measure hit-conditioned semantic divergence. The prober should compute a compact 'susceptibility score' per route/model/config which estimates the probability that a cache hit will change semantic outputs beyond defined thresholds. Additionally produce automated rollback advice (config-level hints) when susceptibility exceeds guardrails to support fast mitigation during rollouts.
background: We've seen intermittent production regressions correlated with prefix cache reuse and config changes (quantization kernels, small model variants). Existing audit suites are heavy and slow; we need a low-overhead continuous probe that produces actionable signals for rollouts and can run in Dedicated/Hosted with minimal cost. This ticket focuses on design and initial implementation of the prober plus an advisor that maps score -> rollback hints.
acceptance_criteria: Prober instrumentation runs at <=1% traffic overhead for selected routes and can be toggled per route via rollout policy
Susceptibility score computed per (route, model, config) and stored in metrics with tags: route, model_version, cache_policy, region
Score thresholds defined (low/medium/high) and documented with example justifications
Rollback advisor generates human-readable hints: e.g., disable-prefetch, reduce-batch-size, fallback-to-variant with lower quantization, or canary-to-non-cached variant
Dashboard in Console that shows top-20 high-susceptibility routes and last 7-day trend
Integration smoke test validates that when we deliberately induce a cache-induced semantic shift (synthetic seed), susceptibility score moves to high and advisor suggests an actionable mitigation
End-to-end demo with a Canary rollout showing advisor-triggered mitigation reduces semantic-delta metric by >=80% in controlled test
tasks: Design susceptibility scoring metric and thresholding (RFC)
Implement lightweight replay path: sample request -> run cached path -> run decached path -> produce diff summary
Token-aware diffing: coarse label (semantic-change/no-change) plus token-level mismatch rate and normalized embedding cosine delta
Add exporter to metrics pipeline (Prometheus + structured logs) with tags
Build advisor logic mapping score + config metadata -> mitigation hints
Create Console dashboard prototype and alerting rule for high-susceptibility routes
Write integration and smoke tests; run controlled synthetic experiments
implementation_notes: Sampling strategy: reservoir-sampled 1% of requests for monitored routes, with stratified sampling by route length buckets
Decached execution must disable all prefix/KV cache reads but keep config identical otherwise (same kernels, quantization paths) to isolate cache effect
Compute two lightweight signals: embedding-cosine-diff on normalized final output embedding and fuzzy-string-similarity on generated text for token-level sensitivity
Use an asynchronous compare pipeline to avoid adding tail latency to live requests; store only compact diffs and metadata
Store raw pairs for 72 hours for debug; purge to limit storage costs
Advisor rules initially rule-based, later incremental ML model considered if false positive rate > 10%
testing_plan: Unit tests for replay harness and decache toggle
Controlled synthetic regression: craft prompts known to be prefix-cache sensitive and validate score increase
Run prober against staging with seeded cache divergences and assert advisor recommendations are in expected set
Load test to verify additional CPU/GPU overhead stays within budget at 1% sampling
Chaos test: flip cache-policy during canary rollout and validate prober detects rising susceptibility and Console alert fires
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Deploy prober to staging routes only and validate outputs (2 days)
Phase 2: Enable 0.5% sampling for a curated set of production routes (week-long observation)
Phase 3: Increase to 1% and enable advisor hints in Console as recommendations (monitor false positives)
Phase 4: Integrate advisor with rollback automation behind an opt-in feature flag for SREs
risks: False positives from embedding-based comparators may cause unnecessary rollbacks
Storage and egress costs if raw pairs are retained too long
Potential privacy concerns when storing raw requests for debugging; need to redact PII
Incorrect decache implementation could change other execution paths and confound attribution
notes: Requested by PMs after a customer incident where quantization config change coincided with observed semantic regressions
Design review scheduled with Runtime and Console teams on 2026-03-05
We should coordinate with Security for PII redaction guidance before enabling raw pair retention in prod
